messages:
Victor N.: hi all, day 1 here. finished the kubectl/kubeconfig steps and can `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` fine on context redwood-dev-west, but `kubectl get secrets -n dev-sandbox` returns Forbidden. Do new hires not get secret access?

Lina C.: welcome Victor! short answer: we don't grant broad secret read access by default. quick check: can you run `kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n dev-sandbox` and `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` and paste results?

Victor N.: output:
```
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox
# -> yes
kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n dev-sandbox
# -> no
```

Lina C.: yep that explains it. infra binds the `redwood:devs` group to a `view` role which allows pods, svc, etc but not secrets. Secrets are restricted; we require an app-level policy or Secrets Team approval. What's the ticket number from infra-bot when you onboarded?

Victor N.: INFRA-12019 was created during onboarding.

infra-bot: INFRA-12019: new-hire RBAC check for victorn. Current: subject group:redwood:devs bound to role:view in namespace=dev-sandbox. To request secret read access, open a request with the Secrets Team and include justification and secret names. See https://intranet.redwood/security/secrets-access.

Victor N.: Ah, ok. I was trying to debug an init container that reads a DB password stored in a secret. Is there a recommended flow for debugging without full secret read perms?

Alex H.: two safe options: 1) ask the Secrets Team for a short-lived, scoped read binding for the specific secret(s) you need (they usually create a RoleBinding for your user or a support serviceaccount for 1-2 hours), 2) ask the app owner to paste the relevant non-sensitive debug values to the ticket or create a temporary ConfigMap with scrubbed values for you. We avoid giving blanket secret permissions to new hires.

Victor N.: filed a Secrets request per infra-bot link: SECRETS-487. included the pod name, secret names (`app-db-creds`, `app-oauth`), and justification (debugging init container failure).

Secrets Team Bot: SECRETS-487 created. Review SLA ~30m. For scoped access we prefer to give `get` on explicit secrets via RoleBinding to user or serviceaccount for a limited duration. Please include your GitHub handle in the ticket.

Victor N.: added GH handle. Meanwhile, can I check logs from the init container without secret access? `kubectl logs -n dev-sandbox pod/app-123 -c init-setup` returned an error referencing "failed to read secret" so logs would help.

Lina C.: logs are usually accessible with your current perms. `kubectl logs -n dev-sandbox pod/app-123 -c init-setup --tail=200` should work if the pod is in the same namespace. If the init container crashes before writing logs, you might need the secret value. If Secrets Team can't provide immediate access, ask infra for a support serviceaccount token bound to those secrets for a short window.

Secrets Team Bot: SECRETS-487 update: approved temporary RoleBinding `verb=get resource=secrets namespace=dev-sandbox subject=user:victorn` for 45 minutes. Please avoid copying secret contents out of the cluster; use them only for debugging. Audit logs will be retained.

Victor N.: thanks — I can `kubectl get secret app-db-creds -n dev-sandbox -o jsonpath='{.data.username}'` now (decoded locally). Resolved the init container config typo. :relieved:

Lina C.: great! quick onboarding notes for docs: 1) default new-hire binding is `view` not `edit`, 2) secret access requires explicit request and justification, 3) prefer temporary scoped RoleBindings or support serviceaccounts for debugging, and 4) always file a SECRETS ticket rather than copying secrets into personal notes. Can you add these to your onboarding feedback?

Victor N.: will do, filing a doc suggestion PR. Also thanks for the safe workflow — surprised how granular RBAC is compared to other places I've worked.

Alex H.: welcome aboard. As a small tip: `kubectl auth can-i --list -n dev-sandbox` shows effective verbs for your user; very handy when verifying what you can do. Also: never run `kubectl get secrets` cluster-wide and avoid copying secret contents into chat.

Secrets Team Bot: SECRETS-487 closed: temporary RoleBinding expired after 45 minutes. No risky behavior detected in audit logs. If you need ongoing access, coordinate with the app owner for an approved permanent role or use a serviceaccount backed pipeline.

Victor N.: all good, thanks everyone! saved the troubleshooting steps in my onboarding notes and the PR includes the secrets-access flow. :tada:
